source.memory: Uncompressed AMSDOS files EXOLON.1 at $0100 (length $6add), EXOLON.2 at $6bdd (length $3424), EXOLON.3 copied from $c000 to $a001 (length $11cc), following the original loader. Other memory is zero. This publicly hosted disk is a cracked release; no claim of a pristine commercial master is made.
source.archiveSearch: CPC-POWER catalog item 54 and CPCRULEZ identify the game; their protected downloads were not used. The Bulba SoLOCPC collection was inspected but did not contain Exolon and supplied no assets.

extraction.ayWriter: $6315 writes register A/value C through CPC PPI $f4xx/$f6xx; captured without replacing the sound instructions or note tables.
extraction.title: Runs the original program from $0100 through its menu/star drawing loop until the music end instruction at $5d20, then calls the original silence routine $5a7c. Keyboard reads are all released; the original PRNG starts with the source-memory seed. Its software-driven update timing is retained by an approximate instruction timer, not replaced by the Spectrum 90 Hz music schedule.
extraction.gameOver: Runs original $2d21–$2d39: silence, $65c6 jingle, 40 driver steps separated by the original $3e54 delay, silence. The text immediately preceding this routine is GAME OVER at $2d65.
extraction.effectTiming: Isolated original effect calls are advanced at 50 driver steps/second, matching the nativeJS presentation convention. The original game calls $63af three times in a variable-duration gameplay loop, so these isolated recordings do not claim original gameplay timing.
extraction.traceFormat: CPCAY001: 8 ASCII magic bytes, little-endian uint32 duration in microseconds, uint32 event count; each 8-byte event is uint32 time, uint8 register, uint8 value, two zero reserved bytes. Traces preserve original register writes. WAV rendering samples register state at 1000 Hz.

offlineRenderer.license: MIT; external offline tool only, no CPU source redistributed or loaded by the game
offlineRenderer.timing: Returned Z80 instruction T-states rounded up to a multiple of four at 4 MHz. This is an approximation, not full CPC machine-cycle contention, PPI/CRTC or hardware capture. Title tempo is consequently approximate; the original CPC pitches, note order, modulation and software volume programs are retained.
offlineRenderer.ay: Repository renderAy at the CPC 1 MHz chip clock, measured AY DAC levels from MIT-licensed Ayumi, 17-bit noise LFSR and 20 Hz AC coupling. Original Exolon CPC captures use software volume envelopes; extraction rejects hardware-envelope volume flags. Mono PCM16 WAV at 44100 Hz.

extraction.reproducePcmWithoutCpu: Copy audio-engine.bin and *.ayr into an output directory, then node tools/audio/cpc.mjs --traces-only --output /tmp/exolon-cpc-audio-output

shot.evidence: Followed by ammo decrement at $115a/$115b. First noise note $0f reads CPC period $0647 from $6b3a.

grenade.evidence: Two simultaneous original effect slots 9 and 15 ($6797 + $6809).

refill-ammo.evidence: Ammo set to 99 at $2672–$2674 immediately before the sound.

refill-grenades.evidence: Grenades set to 10 at $26c8–$26ca immediately before the sound.

suit.evidence: Original changing chamber toggles suit state $2bdb, then calls the same sound as ammo refill.

bonus.evidence: Score-add routine immediately before adding the bonus to pending points at $2bd9.

adaptationAliases.turret: Original explosion/hostile-fire sound $6579; the nativeJS event does not identify which original gun routine produced it.
adaptationAliases.death: Presentation alias to original explosion $6579. The isolated original CPC player-death initializer at $29b4 has no separate sound call; this is not claimed as a recovered death program.
adaptationAliases.suit: Identical to refill-ammo, matching original $6525 calls.

limits: CPC presentation over the shared nativeJS gameplay model. Offline register/PCM captures are software approximations, not recordings from physical hardware. Concurrent voice allocation, effect priority and interruption are captured separately per sound; no Z80 emulator runs in the browser. The previous ZX/C64 recordings and all arrangements are retained.
